page: Vultr vbm-6c-32gb is a bare metal server from the Bare Metal SSD family. It features an Intel Xeon 2286G processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs with dedicated CPU allocation, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, which yields 2.67 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 1920 GB SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 35.51 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.91 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. The PassMark memory score is in the top 10% at 3453.69. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is a notable bottleneck, with read-only speeds at 32.51 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.71 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations score in the average range.

Given its dedicated bare metal resources and high clock speed, the server is suited for workloads requiring consistent CPU performance without virtualization overhead, such as static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database operations. The 1920 GB local SSD offers high-density storage for localized data processing. However, the system is less suited for medium-to-large language model inference, where text generation speeds drop to 7.38 tokens/sec. The hardware profile offers a cost-efficient entry point for dedicated bare metal compute where massive memory bandwidth is not a primary requirement.
